final_report.summary: The StoryForge Observability Mission transformed the AI-StoryForge FastAPI application from a security-hardened but observability-blind service into a production-grade, fully instrumented system. Across 3 cycles, the team built a complete observability stack from scratch using stdlib only: structured JSON logging, security event audit trails, Prometheus-compatible metrics, multi-tier health checks, adaptive log sampling, webhook alerting, audit log rotation, structured error responses, W3C distributed trace context propagation, a circuit breaker for external calls, and per-endpoint rate-limit metrics. The final test suite achieved 120 passing tests (Categories A–Z + LIVE), validating every observability primitive end-to-end. The entire implementation is dependency-free beyond Python's standard library.
all_files: web/audit.py — Audit trail engine: JSONL event recording, webhook alerting with CircuitBreaker, log rotation, async webhook dispatch
web/metrics.py — Prometheus-format /metrics endpoint: total_requests, health_check_total, auth_failures_total, story_generated_total, rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint=...}
web/limiter.py — Rate limiter middleware: per-IP sliding window, per-endpoint 429 counters fed into metrics
web/circuit_breaker.py — Stdlib CircuitBreaker: CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN states, configurable failure threshold + open duration, thread-safe with threading.Lock
web/app.py — Main FastAPI app: request_id middleware extended to W3C traceparent propagation (trace_id + span_id ContextVars), X-Trace-ID / X-Span-ID response headers
web/routes.py — Application routes: /health, /readyz, /metrics, /login, /register, /api/generate with observability hooks
web/admin_routes.py — Admin routes with audit logging for admin actions
tests/test_security_regression.py — Master test suite (Categories A–Z + LIVE): 120 tests covering all observability primitives
OBSERVABILITY_REPORT.md — Complete architecture reference: env vars, endpoint schemas, test coverage summary
key_achievements: 120 tests passing across 27 categories (A–Z + LIVE), 0 failing — full observability stack validated end-to-end
Structured JSON logging: every log line includes timestamp, level, logger, message, request_id, trace_id, span_id, user_id — machine-parseable by ELK/Loki/Splunk
Security audit trail: JSONL-format immutable records for LOGIN_ATTEMPT, LOGIN_SUCCESS, LOGIN_FAILURE, STORY_GENERATED, HEALTH_CHECK, ADMIN_ACTION with user/IP/timestamp

W3C Trace Context propagation (Category W): reads incoming traceparent, re-uses trace-id with new span-id, emits valid traceparent on all responses, injects trace_id+span_id into every log line and audit record
Circuit Breaker (Category X): stdlib CircuitBreaker with CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN state machine, configurable thresholds, thread-safe, integrated with webhook sender in audit.py
Per-endpoint rate-limit metrics (Category Y): rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint='/login'} etc. exposed in Prometheus text format, aggregate counter equals sum of per-endpoint counters
Prometheus /metrics endpoint (Category R): gauge and counter metrics for all key application events, spec-compliant text format
Multi-tier health checks: /health (liveness) and /readyz (readiness) with dependency probes, degraded-mode detection
Adaptive log sampling (Category Q): high-frequency endpoints sampled at configurable rate to control log volume without losing signal
Webhook alerting (Category T) with retry logic and exponential backoff, now protected by CircuitBreaker to prevent cascade failures
Audit log rotation (Category S): configurable max file size and backup count, atomic rotation without data loss
Structured error responses (Category V): all 4xx/5xx responses return JSON with error_code, message, request_id, trace_id
challenges_overcome: W3C traceparent parsing edge cases: malformed headers (wrong version prefix, non-hex trace-id, wrong segment count) must all be silently treated as absent and a fresh trace generated — required careful regex validation before acceptance

CircuitBreaker HALF_OPEN probe semantics: exactly one concurrent probe request must be allowed while all others fast-fail — solved with a threading.Lock + in_probe flag to prevent thundering herd on recovery

Rate-limit counter threading: per-endpoint counters incremented from middleware must be safe under concurrent request load — used threading.Lock in limiter.py shared with metrics.py via module-level registry
Prometheus label syntax: the spec requires labels in {key="value"} format with escaped quotes — test suite validates exact format string matching, required careful f-string construction in metrics.py

Category Z integration test startup timing: the test spins up the actual FastAPI app on port 5100, fires 50 mixed requests, then reads audit.jsonl — required robust port-wait logic and proper tmpdir isolation so test runs don't collide with each other
Audit trail completeness under sampling: log sampling must not discard audit records — audit.py writes directly to the JSONL file bypassing the sampling filter, ensuring 100% audit record fidelity

ContextVar propagation through async middleware: trace_id and span_id must flow from the ASGI middleware layer into every downstream coroutine — used contextvars.ContextVar with proper token reset in finally blocks
lessons_learned: Stdlib-only constraint forces cleaner designs: without httpx or requests, the webhook sender had to use urllib.request — this actually made the circuit breaker integration cleaner because there was only one call site to wrap
Test categories as a design specification: defining A–Z categories upfront created a forcing function that prevented scope creep and kept each implementation focused on a single observable property

ContextVar reset discipline is critical in async ASGI: forgetting to reset ContextVar tokens in finally blocks causes trace context to bleed between requests in the same worker thread — always use try/finally around set()

Circuit breaker probe must be atomic: using a simple boolean flag without a lock causes two threads to simultaneously see HALF_OPEN and both attempt probes — the lock must gate the probe decision, not just the state read

Prometheus text format is stricter than it looks: trailing newlines, label quoting, and the HELP/TYPE comment ordering all matter for real scrapers — write a format validator test early and run it against every metrics change

Per-endpoint rate limit tracking belongs in the rate limiter, not the route handler: placing the increment in limiter.py means it fires for every 429 regardless of which route triggered it, and the route handlers stay clean
Audit log rotation must be tested with real file I/O: mocking the RotatingFileHandler masks bugs in the size calculation — use a real tmpdir with a tiny max_bytes to force rotation in the test
